name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
The system is a web portal designed to support people who want to organize an event by bringing together, in a single platform, information about event guests and the various services required for the event.

The platform supports three main types of users: event organizers, service providers, and invited guests.

Service providers register on the platform by providing authentication credentials, personal information, and company details, including VAT number, company address, and accepted payment methods.

Once registered, providers can publish the services offered by their company. Each service belongs to a category, such as catering, hairdressing, florist services, or transportation. For each service, the provider can configure a virtual showcase containing demonstration photos, prices, and the time slots during which the service is available.

Event organizers register by providing credentials, personal information, residence information, their fiscal code, and an IBAN that can be used for service payments.

Through the portal, organizers can create an event by specifying the event type, date, location, and the planned budget. During event creation, they can also select from a predefined list the categories of services for which they want to receive support.

Organizers can add invited guests to the event by entering their personal information, email address, and guest category, such as relative, friend, or colleague. For each invited guest, the system generates an invitation code that is sent by email and is used by the guest as a password to access the platform.

Each event has an associated blog where both organizers and invited guests can publish information about the event, upload photos or videos, create new posts, and comment on existing posts.

After creating an event, the organizer can browse the service showcases provided by suppliers for the selected service categories. The organizer can then request an appointment with a provider by choosing a time compatible with the provider's availability and specifying appointment details and any special requests.

Providers can view appointment requests through their interface and decide whether to approve them. Approved appointments are automatically displayed in a calendar associated with the event, which the organizer can consult to view all confirmed service appointments.

After an appointment between the organizer and the provider has taken place, the provider prepares a quotation for the agreed service and uploads the corresponding amount to the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once a quotation has been uploaded, the organizer can accept or reject it. If the quotation is accepted, its total amount is deducted from the remaining event budget.

When accepting a quotation, the organizer selects both the payment schedule, which can consist of installments, deposit plus final balance, or full payment, and the payment method, which can be online or on-site.

If payment is made on-site, the provider confirms the received amount through the portal. If payment is divided into multiple installments, the provider confirms each received installment separately.

At any time, the organizer can consult the history of contracts associated with the event, including their status and cost, and can also view the remaining event budget.

highLevelGoals: Allow event organizers to efficiently plan, manage, and coordinate all aspects of an event, including guest invitations, service bookings, and budget tracking.
Provide a centralized platform where event organizers can discover, select, and book event-related services from verified providers.
Support secure, flexible, and traceable payment transactions between organizers and service providers, including installment payments and on-site confirmations.
Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and manage their services with detailed information, pricing, and availability.
Allow service providers to respond to appointment requests, generate quotations, and confirm payments received for completed services.
Allow invited guests to access event-related content, such as blogs and photos, using invitation codes for secure access.
Enable both organizers and invited guests to contribute to event blogs by posting, uploading media, and commenting on event-related content.
Enable event organizers to view the history of contracts associated with their events, including status and cost, as well as the remaining event budget.
lowLevelGoals: The event organizer inputs event name, date, location, and budget via a form interface.
The event organizer generates and distributes unique invitation codes to guests via email or messaging.
The event organizer searches and filters services by category, price, and availability, then selects one for booking.
The event organizer confirms booking and selects payment method (e.g., one-time, installment, on-site) for the service.
The event organizer accesses a list of past contracts with status, cost, and completion details.
The event organizer checks the current remaining budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses.
The service provider uploads service details, including description, pricing, and availability, to the platform.
The service provider assigns categories and tags to their services for better discoverability by event organizers.
The service provider accepts or declines appointment requests from event organizers via the platform.
The service provider creates and sends a quotation to the event organizer with pricing and terms.
The service provider marks a service as completed and confirms receipt of payment from the event organizer.
The invited guest enters an invitation code to gain secure access to event-related content.
The invited guest browses and views event-related blogs and photos after successful authentication via invitation code.
The invited guest submits a blog post or media upload to the event’s public or private blog section.
The invited guest uploads images or videos to the event blog for sharing with other guests.
The invited guest leaves a comment on an existing blog post to engage with other participants.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are appropriate and representative of the system's description. No contradictions or omissions were found.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are mostly representative of the software system's description. However, there is a slight omission regarding the ability for event organizers to select predefined service categories during event creation, which is mentioned in the description but not explicitly covered as a goal. Additionally, the goal about invited guests contributing to event blogs seems inconsistent with the description, which primarily focuses on event planning and service coordination rather than collaborative content creation.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-aligned with the high-level goals and actors, covering all necessary functional aspects of the system. There are no contradictions or omissions, and each goal corresponds to a specific action an actor can perform on the software.

Together, these LLGs define a system for event setup and guest invitation management, with no inferred or generalized functionality beyond what is explicitly stated.

No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system is a web portal designed to support people who want to organize an event by bringing together, in a single platform, information about event guests and the various services required for the event.

The platform supports three main types of users: event organizers, service providers, and invited guests.

Service providers register on the platform by providing authentication credentials, personal information, and company details, including VAT number, company address, and accepted payment methods.

Once registered, providers can publish the services offered by their company. Each service belongs to a category, such as catering, hairdressing, florist services, or transportation. For each service, the provider can configure a virtual showcase containing demonstration photos, prices, and the time slots during which the service is available.

Event organizers register by providing credentials, personal information, residence information, their fiscal code, and an IBAN that can be used for service payments.

Through the portal, organizers can create an event by specifying the event type, date, location, and the planned budget. During event creation, they can also select from a predefined list the categories of services for which they want to receive support.

Organizers can add invited guests to the event by entering their personal information, email address, and guest category, such as relative, friend, or colleague. For each invited guest, the system generates an invitation code that is sent by email and is used by the guest as a password to access the platform.

Each event has an associated blog where both organizers and invited guests can publish information about the event, upload photos or videos, create new posts, and comment on existing posts.

After creating an event, the organizer can browse the service showcases provided by suppliers for the selected service categories. The organizer can then request an appointment with a provider by choosing a time compatible with the provider's availability and specifying appointment details and any special requests.

Providers can view appointment requests through their interface and decide whether to approve them. Approved appointments are automatically displayed in a calendar associated with the event, which the organizer can consult to view all confirmed service appointments.

After an appointment between the organizer and the provider has taken place, the provider prepares a quotation for the agreed service and uploads the corresponding amount to the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once a quotation has been uploaded, the organizer can accept or reject it. If the quotation is accepted, its total amount is deducted from the remaining event budget.

When accepting a quotation, the organizer selects both the payment schedule, which can consist of installments, deposit plus final balance, or full payment, and the payment method, which can be online or on-site.

If payment is made on-site, the provider confirms the received amount through the portal. If payment is divided into multiple installments, the provider confirms each received installment separately.

At any time, the organizer can consult the history of contracts associated with the event, including their status and cost, and can also view the remaining event budget.

hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to configure event details including name, date, location, and budget; llg_002 adds the capability to generate unique, cryptographically secure invitation codes per guest; llg_003 adds the capability to automatically distribute those codes via email to guests’ registered email addresses.

hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to browse, filter, select, and book event services based on category, price, and availability.
hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to browse and select event services by filtering on category, price, and availability, and to initiate booking. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

hlg_05de50bd78f85f93_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to discover, book, manage financial commitments for, and monitor service contracts within an event’s budget.
hlg_05de50bd78f85f93_001.rationale: llg_001 enables discovery and filtering of service showcases by category, which supports initial selection. llg_002 enables booking appointments with providers by selecting time and details, which supports service acquisition. llg_003 enables acceptance of quotations and selection of payment terms (schedule and method), which manages financial obligations. llg_004 enables viewing contract history and remaining budget, which supports ongoing financial oversight. Together, these cover the full lifecycle of service procurement and financial management for event organizers, including discovery, booking, payment configuration, and budget tracking.

hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and tag their offerings for discoverability and availability on the platform.
hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.rationale: llg_001 enables service providers to publish service offerings by uploading details such as description, pricing, and availability; llg_002 enables them to categorize and tag services to enhance discoverability by event organizers. Together, these capabilities form a complete scope for service publication and metadata management, with no unrelated or broader capabilities introduced.

hlg_94df30668f000172_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide a complete service lifecycle for event organizers, including responding to appointment requests, generating and sending quotations, and confirming payment receipt for completed services.
hlg_94df30668f000172_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to respond to appointment requests by accepting or declining them via the platform. llg_002 adds the capability to generate and send quotations with pricing and terms to event organizers. llg_003 adds the capability to confirm payment receipt after service completion, marking the service as done. These three distinct lifecycle phases — request handling, quotation generation, and payment confirmation — are all required and must be explicitly included in the reconstructed goal to preserve their material differences and avoid generalization.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm payment receipt for completed services

hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to securely access and view event-related content, including blogs and photos, by authenticating via an invitation code.
hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.rationale: llg_001 enables secure access to event content using an invitation code, which is the authentication mechanism. llg_002 extends this by allowing the guest to view specific content types (blogs and photos) after authentication. Together, they define a complete scope: secure access via invitation code and subsequent viewing of event blogs and photos — no other capabilities are implied or inferred.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Access event content using invitation code

hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to contribute content, media, and feedback to an event blog through posting, uploading, and commenting.
hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.rationale: llg_001 enables content submission (posting blog posts or media), llg_002 enables media uploading (images or videos), and llg_003 enables interaction (commenting on posts). Together, they cover the full scope of content contribution and engagement via the event blog, with no hidden or inferred functionality.

hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to view and manage contract history while simultaneously monitoring the remaining event budget to ensure financial accountability and operational oversight.
hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the event organizer to view and manage contract history, including status, cost, and completion details, which supports historical tracking and contractual accountability. llg_002 enables the organizer to view the remaining event budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses, which supports real-time financial monitoring. Together, these capabilities form a dual-track system: one for contract lifecycle visibility and one for budgetary control — no other capability is implied or inferred, and both are explicitly preserved.

hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Create and distribute event invitations by configuring event details, generating unique cryptographically secure invitation codes for guests, and automatically sending those codes via email.
hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to configure event details including name, date, location, and budget; llg_002 adds the capability to generate unique, cryptographically secure invitation codes per guest; llg_003 adds the capability to automatically distribute those codes via email to guests’ registered email addresses.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Generate unique invitation codes for guests

hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to browse, filter, select, and book event services based on category, price, and availability.
hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to browse and select event services by filtering on category, price, and availability, and to initiate booking. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and tag their offerings for discoverability and availability on the platform.
hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.rationale: llg_001 enables service providers to publish service offerings by uploading details such as description, pricing, and availability; llg_002 enables them to categorize and tag services to enhance discoverability by event organizers. Together, these capabilities form a complete scope for service publication and metadata management, with no unrelated or broader capabilities introduced.

hlg_94df30668f000172_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide a complete service lifecycle for event organizers, including responding to appointment requests, generating and sending quotations, and confirming payment receipt for completed services.
hlg_94df30668f000172_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to respond to appointment requests by accepting or declining them via the platform. llg_002 adds the capability to generate and send quotations with pricing and terms to event organizers. llg_003 adds the capability to confirm payment receipt after service completion, marking the service as done. These three distinct lifecycle phases — request handling, quotation generation, and payment confirmation — are all required and must be explicitly included in the reconstructed goal to preserve their material differences and avoid generalization.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm payment receipt for completed services

hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to securely access and view event-related content, including blogs and photos, by authenticating via an invitation code.
hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.rationale: llg_001 enables secure access to event content using an invitation code, which is the authentication mechanism. llg_002 extends this by allowing the guest to view specific content types (blogs and photos) after authentication. Together, they define a complete scope: secure access via invitation code and subsequent viewing of event blogs and photos — no other capabilities are implied or inferred.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Access event content using invitation code

hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to contribute content, media, and feedback to an event blog through posting, uploading, and commenting.
hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.rationale: llg_001 enables content submission (posting blog posts or media), llg_002 enables media uploading (images or videos), and llg_003 enables interaction (commenting on posts). Together, they cover the full scope of content contribution and engagement via the event blog, with no hidden or inferred functionality.

hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to view and manage contract history while simultaneously monitoring the remaining event budget to ensure financial accountability and operational oversight.
hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the event organizer to view and manage contract history, including status, cost, and completion details, which supports historical tracking and contractual accountability. llg_002 enables the organizer to view the remaining event budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses, which supports real-time financial monitoring. Together, these capabilities form a dual-track system: one for contract lifecycle visibility and one for budgetary control — no other capability is implied or inferred, and both are explicitly preserved.

hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to browse, filter, select, and book event services based on category, price, and availability.
hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to browse and select event services by filtering on category, price, and availability, and to initiate booking. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and tag their offerings for discoverability and availability on the platform.
hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.rationale: llg_001 enables service providers to publish service offerings by uploading details such as description, pricing, and availability; llg_002 enables them to categorize and tag services to enhance discoverability by event organizers. Together, these capabilities form a complete scope for service publication and metadata management, with no unrelated or broader capabilities introduced.

hlg_94df30668f000172_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide a complete service lifecycle for event organizers, including responding to appointment requests, generating and sending quotations, and confirming payment receipt for completed services.
hlg_94df30668f000172_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to respond to appointment requests by accepting or declining them via the platform. llg_002 adds the capability to generate and send quotations with pricing and terms to event organizers. llg_003 adds the capability to confirm payment receipt after service completion, marking the service as done. These three distinct lifecycle phases — request handling, quotation generation, and payment confirmation — are all required and must be explicitly included in the reconstructed goal to preserve their material differences and avoid generalization.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm payment receipt for completed services

hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to securely access and view event-related content, including blogs and photos, by authenticating via an invitation code.
hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.rationale: llg_001 enables secure access to event content using an invitation code, which is the authentication mechanism. llg_002 extends this by allowing the guest to view specific content types (blogs and photos) after authentication. Together, they define a complete scope: secure access via invitation code and subsequent viewing of event blogs and photos — no other capabilities are implied or inferred.

hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to contribute content, media, and feedback to an event blog through posting, uploading, and commenting.
hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.rationale: llg_001 enables content submission (posting blog posts or media), llg_002 enables media uploading (images or videos), and llg_003 enables interaction (commenting on posts). Together, they cover the full scope of content contribution and engagement via the event blog, with no hidden or inferred functionality.

hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to view and manage contract history while simultaneously monitoring the remaining event budget to ensure financial accountability and operational oversight.
hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the event organizer to view and manage contract history, including status, cost, and completion details, which supports historical tracking and contractual accountability. llg_002 enables the organizer to view the remaining event budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses, which supports real-time financial monitoring. Together, these capabilities form a dual-track system: one for contract lifecycle visibility and one for budgetary control — no other capability is implied or inferred, and both are explicitly preserved.

hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to manage appointment requests, generate and send associated quotations, and confirm payment receipts for completed services via a digital platform.
hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the service provider to handle incoming appointment requests by accepting or declining them; llg_002 enables the creation and association of quotations with approved appointments and events; llg_003 enables the service provider to confirm payment receipt for completed services, either fully or in installments. Together, these cover the lifecycle of service engagement from request to payment confirmation, with no implicit or inferred functionality beyond these three distinct capabilities.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system is a web portal designed to support people who want to organize an event by bringing together, in a single platform, information about event guests and the various services required for the event.

The platform supports three main types of users: event organizers, service providers, and invited guests.

Service providers register on the platform by providing authentication credentials, personal information, and company details, including VAT number, company address, and accepted payment methods.

Once registered, providers can publish the services offered by their company. Each service belongs to a category, such as catering, hairdressing, florist services, or transportation. For each service, the provider can configure a virtual showcase containing demonstration photos, prices, and the time slots during which the service is available.

Event organizers register by providing credentials, personal information, residence information, their fiscal code, and an IBAN that can be used for service payments.

Through the portal, organizers can create an event by specifying the event type, date, location, and the planned budget. During event creation, they can also select from a predefined list the categories of services for which they want to receive support.

Organizers can add invited guests to the event by entering their personal information, email address, and guest category, such as relative, friend, or colleague. For each invited guest, the system generates an invitation code that is sent by email and is used by the guest as a password to access the platform.

Each event has an associated blog where both organizers and invited guests can publish information about the event, upload photos or videos, create new posts, and comment on existing posts.

After creating an event, the organizer can browse the service showcases provided by suppliers for the selected service categories. The organizer can then request an appointment with a provider by choosing a time compatible with the provider's availability and specifying appointment details and any special requests.

Providers can view appointment requests through their interface and decide whether to approve them. Approved appointments are automatically displayed in a calendar associated with the event, which the organizer can consult to view all confirmed service appointments.

After an appointment between the organizer and the provider has taken place, the provider prepares a quotation for the agreed service and uploads the corresponding amount to the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once a quotation has been uploaded, the organizer can accept or reject it. If the quotation is accepted, its total amount is deducted from the remaining event budget.

When accepting a quotation, the organizer selects both the payment schedule, which can consist of installments, deposit plus final balance, or full payment, and the payment method, which can be online or on-site.

If payment is made on-site, the provider confirms the received amount through the portal. If payment is divided into multiple installments, the provider confirms each received installment separately.

At any time, the organizer can consult the history of contracts associated with the event, including their status and cost, and can also view the remaining event budget.

hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Create and distribute event invitations by configuring event details, generating unique cryptographically secure invitation codes for guests, and automatically sending those codes via email.
hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to configure event details including name, date, location, and budget; llg_002 adds the capability to generate unique, cryptographically secure invitation codes per guest; llg_003 adds the capability to automatically distribute those codes via email to guests’ registered email addresses.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Generate unique invitation codes for guests

hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to browse, filter, select, and book event services based on category, price, and availability.
hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to browse and select event services by filtering on category, price, and availability, and to initiate booking. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and tag their offerings for discoverability and availability on the platform.
hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.rationale: llg_001 enables service providers to publish service offerings by uploading details such as description, pricing, and availability; llg_002 enables them to categorize and tag services to enhance discoverability by event organizers. Together, these capabilities form a complete scope for service publication and metadata management, with no unrelated or broader capabilities introduced.

hlg_94df30668f000172_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide a complete service lifecycle for event organizers, including responding to appointment requests, generating and sending quotations, and confirming payment receipt for completed services.
hlg_94df30668f000172_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to respond to appointment requests by accepting or declining them via the platform. llg_002 adds the capability to generate and send quotations with pricing and terms to event organizers. llg_003 adds the capability to confirm payment receipt after service completion, marking the service as done. These three distinct lifecycle phases — request handling, quotation generation, and payment confirmation — are all required and must be explicitly included in the reconstructed goal to preserve their material differences and avoid generalization.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm payment receipt for completed services

hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to securely access and view event-related content, including blogs and photos, by authenticating via an invitation code.
hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.rationale: llg_001 enables secure access to event content using an invitation code, which is the authentication mechanism. llg_002 extends this by allowing the guest to view specific content types (blogs and photos) after authentication. Together, they define a complete scope: secure access via invitation code and subsequent viewing of event blogs and photos — no other capabilities are implied or inferred.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Access event content using invitation code

hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to contribute content, media, and feedback to an event blog through posting, uploading, and commenting.
hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.rationale: llg_001 enables content submission (posting blog posts or media), llg_002 enables media uploading (images or videos), and llg_003 enables interaction (commenting on posts). Together, they cover the full scope of content contribution and engagement via the event blog, with no hidden or inferred functionality.

hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to view and manage contract history while simultaneously monitoring the remaining event budget to ensure financial accountability and operational oversight.
hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the event organizer to view and manage contract history, including status, cost, and completion details, which supports historical tracking and contractual accountability. llg_002 enables the organizer to view the remaining event budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses, which supports real-time financial monitoring. Together, these capabilities form a dual-track system: one for contract lifecycle visibility and one for budgetary control — no other capability is implied or inferred, and both are explicitly preserved.

hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to manage appointment requests, generate and send associated quotations, and confirm payment receipts for completed services via a digital platform.
hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the service provider to handle incoming appointment requests by accepting or declining them; llg_002 enables the creation and association of quotations with approved appointments and events; llg_003 enables the service provider to confirm payment receipt for completed services, either fully or in installments. Together, these cover the lifecycle of service engagement from request to payment confirmation, with no implicit or inferred functionality beyond these three distinct capabilities.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm payment receipt for completed services

hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Create and distribute event invitations by configuring event details, generating unique cryptographically secure invitation codes for guests, and automatically sending those codes via email.
hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to configure event details including name, date, location, and budget; llg_002 adds the capability to generate unique, cryptographically secure invitation codes per guest; llg_003 adds the capability to automatically distribute those codes via email to guests’ registered email addresses.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Generate unique invitation codes for guests

hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to browse, filter, select, and book event services based on category, price, and availability.
hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to browse and select event services by filtering on category, price, and availability, and to initiate booking. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and tag their offerings for discoverability and availability on the platform.
hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.rationale: llg_001 enables service providers to publish service offerings by uploading details such as description, pricing, and availability; llg_002 enables them to categorize and tag services to enhance discoverability by event organizers. Together, these capabilities form a complete scope for service publication and metadata management, with no unrelated or broader capabilities introduced.

hlg_94df30668f000172_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Provide a complete service lifecycle for event organizers, including responding to appointment requests, generating and sending quotations, and confirming payment receipt for completed services.
hlg_94df30668f000172_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to respond to appointment requests by accepting or declining them via the platform. llg_002 adds the capability to generate and send quotations with pricing and terms to event organizers. llg_003 adds the capability to confirm payment receipt after service completion, marking the service as done. These three distinct lifecycle phases — request handling, quotation generation, and payment confirmation — are all required and must be explicitly included in the reconstructed goal to preserve their material differences and avoid generalization.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm payment receipt for completed services

hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to securely access and view event-related content, including blogs and photos, by authenticating via an invitation code.
hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.rationale: llg_001 enables secure access to event content using an invitation code, which is the authentication mechanism. llg_002 extends this by allowing the guest to view specific content types (blogs and photos) after authentication. Together, they define a complete scope: secure access via invitation code and subsequent viewing of event blogs and photos — no other capabilities are implied or inferred.

hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to contribute content, media, and feedback to an event blog through posting, uploading, and commenting.

hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to view and manage contract history while simultaneously monitoring the remaining event budget to ensure financial accountability and operational oversight.
hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the event organizer to view and manage contract history, including status, cost, and completion details, which supports historical tracking and contractual accountability. llg_002 enables the organizer to view the remaining event budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses, which supports real-time financial monitoring. Together, these capabilities form a dual-track system: one for contract lifecycle visibility and one for budgetary control — no other capability is implied or inferred, and both are explicitly preserved.

hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to manage appointment requests, generate and send associated quotations, and confirm payment receipts for completed services via a digital platform.
hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the service provider to handle incoming appointment requests by accepting or declining them; llg_002 enables the creation and association of quotations with approved appointments and events; llg_003 enables the service provider to confirm payment receipt for completed services, either fully or in installments. Together, these cover the lifecycle of service engagement from request to payment confirmation, with no implicit or inferred functionality beyond these three distinct capabilities.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system is a web portal designed to support people who want to organize an event by bringing together, in a single platform, information about event guests and the various services required for the event.

The platform supports three main types of users: event organizers, service providers, and invited guests.

Service providers register on the platform by providing authentication credentials, personal information, and company details, including VAT number, company address, and accepted payment methods.

Once registered, providers can publish the services offered by their company. Each service belongs to a category, such as catering, hairdressing, florist services, or transportation. For each service, the provider can configure a virtual showcase containing demonstration photos, prices, and the time slots during which the service is available.

Event organizers register by providing credentials, personal information, residence information, their fiscal code, and an IBAN that can be used for service payments.

Through the portal, organizers can create an event by specifying the event type, date, location, and the planned budget. During event creation, they can also select from a predefined list the categories of services for which they want to receive support.

Organizers can add invited guests to the event by entering their personal information, email address, and guest category, such as relative, friend, or colleague. For each invited guest, the system generates an invitation code that is sent by email and is used by the guest as a password to access the platform.

Each event has an associated blog where both organizers and invited guests can publish information about the event, upload photos or videos, create new posts, and comment on existing posts.

After creating an event, the organizer can browse the service showcases provided by suppliers for the selected service categories. The organizer can then request an appointment with a provider by choosing a time compatible with the provider's availability and specifying appointment details and any special requests.

Providers can view appointment requests through their interface and decide whether to approve them. Approved appointments are automatically displayed in a calendar associated with the event, which the organizer can consult to view all confirmed service appointments.

After an appointment between the organizer and the provider has taken place, the provider prepares a quotation for the agreed service and uploads the corresponding amount to the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once a quotation has been uploaded, the organizer can accept or reject it. If the quotation is accepted, its total amount is deducted from the remaining event budget.

When accepting a quotation, the organizer selects both the payment schedule, which can consist of installments, deposit plus final balance, or full payment, and the payment method, which can be online or on-site.

If payment is made on-site, the provider confirms the received amount through the portal. If payment is divided into multiple installments, the provider confirms each received installment separately.

At any time, the organizer can consult the history of contracts associated with the event, including their status and cost, and can also view the remaining event budget.

hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to browse and select event services by filtering on category, price, and availability, and to initiate booking. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and tag their offerings for discoverability and availability on the platform.
hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.rationale: llg_001 enables service providers to publish service offerings by uploading details such as description, pricing, and availability; llg_002 enables them to categorize and tag services to enhance discoverability by event organizers. Together, these capabilities form a complete scope for service publication and metadata management, with no unrelated or broader capabilities introduced.

hlg_68151bcdd8d528e7_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to manage appointment requests from event organizers, generate and upload quotations for approved appointments, and confirm receipt of full or installment payments for completed services.
hlg_68151bcdd8d528e7_001.rationale: llg_001 enables viewing incoming appointment requests; llg_002 enables approving or rejecting those requests; llg_003 enables generating detailed quotations for approved appointments; llg_004 enables uploading those quotations to the platform; llg_005 enables confirming receipt of full payment for completed services; llg_006 enables confirming receipt of installment payments for services paid in installments. Each LLG contributes a distinct functional capability, including the handling of installment payments, which is materially different from full payment confirmation.

hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to securely access and view event-related content, including blogs and photos, by authenticating via an invitation code.
hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.rationale: llg_001 enables secure access to event content using an invitation code, which is the authentication mechanism. llg_002 extends this by allowing the guest to view specific content types (blogs and photos) after authentication. Together, they define a complete scope: secure access via invitation code and subsequent viewing of event blogs and photos — no other capabilities are implied or inferred.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Access event content using invitation code

hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to contribute content, media, and feedback to an event blog through posting, uploading, and commenting.
hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.rationale: llg_001 enables content submission (posting blog posts or media), llg_002 enables media uploading (images or videos), and llg_003 enables interaction (commenting on posts). Together, they cover the full scope of content contribution and engagement via the event blog, with no hidden or inferred functionality.

hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to view and manage contract history while simultaneously monitoring the remaining event budget to ensure financial accountability and operational oversight.
hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the event organizer to view and manage contract history, including status, cost, and completion details, which supports historical tracking and contractual accountability. llg_002 enables the organizer to view the remaining event budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses, which supports real-time financial monitoring. Together, these capabilities form a dual-track system: one for contract lifecycle visibility and one for budgetary control — no other capability is implied or inferred, and both are explicitly preserved.

hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to manage appointment requests, generate and send associated quotations, and confirm payment receipts for completed services via a digital platform.
hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the service provider to handle incoming appointment requests by accepting or declining them; llg_002 enables the creation and association of quotations with approved appointments and events; llg_003 enables the service provider to confirm payment receipt for completed services, either fully or in installments. Together, these cover the lifecycle of service engagement from request to payment confirmation, with no implicit or inferred functionality beyond these three distinct capabilities.

hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Create and distribute event invitations by configuring event details, generating unique cryptographically secure invitation codes for guests, and automatically sending those codes via email.
hlg_d8e5259c55bea167_001.rationale: llg_001 adds the capability to configure event details including name, date, location, and budget; llg_002 adds the capability to generate unique, cryptographically secure invitation codes per guest; llg_003 adds the capability to automatically distribute those codes via email to guests’ registered email addresses.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Generate unique invitation codes for guests

hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to browse, filter, select, and book event services based on category, price, and availability.
hlg_dc05a6a00e807452_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability to browse and select event services by filtering on category, price, and availability, and to initiate booking. No other LLGs are provided, so the reconstructed goal encompasses only this single capability without adding or omitting any detail.

hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to publish, categorize, and tag their offerings for discoverability and availability on the platform.
hlg_bba1d36093273738_001.rationale: llg_001 enables service providers to publish service offerings by uploading details such as description, pricing, and availability; llg_002 enables them to categorize and tag services to enhance discoverability by event organizers. Together, these capabilities form a complete scope for service publication and metadata management, with no unrelated or broader capabilities introduced.

hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to securely access and view event-related content, including blogs and photos, by authenticating via an invitation code.
hlg_57dbb1d19d575603_001.rationale: llg_001 enables secure access to event content using an invitation code, which is the authentication mechanism. llg_002 extends this by allowing the guest to view specific content types (blogs and photos) after authentication. Together, they define a complete scope: secure access via invitation code and subsequent viewing of event blogs and photos — no other capabilities are implied or inferred.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Access event content using invitation code

hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable invited guests to contribute content, media, and feedback to an event blog through posting, uploading, and commenting.
hlg_d4bd8d89225ca214_001.rationale: llg_001 enables content submission (posting blog posts or media), llg_002 enables media uploading (images or videos), and llg_003 enables interaction (commenting on posts). Together, they cover the full scope of content contribution and engagement via the event blog, with no hidden or inferred functionality.

hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable event organizers to view and manage contract history while simultaneously monitoring the remaining event budget to ensure financial accountability and operational oversight.
hlg_e2c0b7b29ea3a654_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the event organizer to view and manage contract history, including status, cost, and completion details, which supports historical tracking and contractual accountability. llg_002 enables the organizer to view the remaining event budget after accounting for all booked services and expenses, which supports real-time financial monitoring. Together, these capabilities form a dual-track system: one for contract lifecycle visibility and one for budgetary control — no other capability is implied or inferred, and both are explicitly preserved.

hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable service providers to manage appointment requests, generate and send associated quotations, and confirm payment receipts for completed services via a digital platform.
hlg_28a65a586c094f31_001.rationale: llg_001 enables the service provider to handle incoming appointment requests by accepting or declining them; llg_002 enables the creation and association of quotations with approved appointments and events; llg_003 enables the service provider to confirm payment receipt for completed services, either fully or in installments. Together, these cover the lifecycle of service engagement from request to payment confirmation, with no implicit or inferred functionality beyond these three distinct capabilities.
source_low_level_goal_ids: Confirm payment receipt for completed services
